articles.headline: Micah Parsons wants to ensure 'all the small things fixed first' before return
articles.description: The Packers' Micah Parsons explained on his podcast why he's not rushing his return from last season's knee injury.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Packers star edge rusher Micah Parsons won't play Sunday against his former team, the Dallas Cowboys, but he said on his podcast that if this was Super Bowl week, he would play.

Parsons has not yet returned to practice since last season's torn ACL and meniscus and remains on the physically unable to perform list.

"The biggest thing that people worried about with me, they're like, 'Man, why ain't he back yet?'" Parsons said on the latest episode of podcast, "The Edge with Micah Parsons," released this week.

"If the Super Bowl was this week, I'm playing in the Super Bowl. But it's just about me making sure I have all the small things fixed first. What a lot of people don't figure out is it's not just the ACL. It's like, why did the ACL happen? What was weak? Because it all works together. It's a chain. And throughout the history of ACL, they notice if you come back early, there tends to be an overcompensation injury on the other side."

Parsons said he wants to make sure everything is right before he gets back on the field.

"It's like, what's the point of getting me back for four weeks and then next thing you know, my groin [is] bothering me," he said.

Earlier in the week, Packers coach Matt LaFleur said they're still waiting for Parsons to be medically cleared.

"He's a physical specimen, he's a creature of nature for sure and sometimes you've got to make sure that your body is, I guess, what's the word I'm looking for? Everything is just [in sync]," LaFleur said. "You don't want one leg to be that much stronger than the other leg is what I'm getting at."

Parsons was injured on Dec. 14 and had surgery on Dec. 29. The Packers typically hold out players coming back from ACL surgery for at least nine months. Parsons is about 9½ months removed from surgery.

Parsons had said during training camp this summer that he thought a return against his former team in Week 6 was "very realistic."

"So many people wanted me to be back for that game to make the game bigger than what it was," Parsons said on his podcast. "It's just another 'Sunday Night Football' game between two good teams. It's not about me. I think that probably let people down. 'Oh, Micah, he's gonna want to be back for the Dallas game.' No, I'm in that phase of life where I just want to be healthy again. That's it."

articles.headline: Source: Lamar Jackson has realistic chance to play Ravens' Week 6 game at Browns
articles.description: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has a realistic chance to return for Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns, a league source told ESPN.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has a realistic chance to return for Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns, a league source told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Jackson missed Baltimore's Week 5 victory over the Atlanta Falcons because of a sprained left ankle.

Sources told ESPN last week that Jackson, despite the injury, still had a slim chance to play against the Falcons. Ravens coach Jesse Minter also indicated last week that Jackson was working toward a quick return.

Jackson suffered the injury during Baltimore's Week 4 victory against the Tennessee Titans. The two-time NFL MVP did not play in the second half of that game and left the stadium in a walking boot.

With Jackson sidelined, Tyler "Snoop" Huntley rallied the Ravens to a 30-23 overtime victory Sunday night in Atlanta. Huntley threw the game-tying touchdown pass to Devontez Walker with 40 seconds remaining in regulation before scoring the game-winning touchdown in overtime on a 1-yard run.

Huntley completed 24 of 32 passes against the Falcons for 201 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing for 20 yards on six carries.

With Jackson as their starting quarterback, the Ravens are 79-32 (.712), averaging 28.4 points per game. Without Jackson since the start of the 2019 season, Baltimore is 7-11.

articles.headline: Mikel Merino says Arsenal are 'ready' for Premier League, Champions League double
articles.description: Mikel Merino insists Arsenal are ready to go one better than last season and complete a Premier League and Champions League double.
articles.body:
Mikel Merino insists Arsenal are ready to go one better than last season and complete a Premier League and Champions League double.

Off the back of taking their first league title in 22 years, the Gunners have started this season with nine victories from 10 matches.

Arsenal's sole blemish so far arrived in a shock 3-0 defeat at Brighton which leaves them three points behind Manchester City in the Premier League. Mikel Arteta's men saw off Lille on Tuesday night to make it two wins from two in the Champions League.

The European triumph marked Arsenal's 14th consecutive victory in the group stage of the competition. The Gunners missed out on Champions League glory last term following an agonising penalty shootout defeat to Paris St Germain.

"It is an absolutely unbelievable run," said Merino of Arsenal's winning streak which stands at almost two years. "We know that we're making history.

"At the same time, we know how difficult it is to win games, so we give a lot of value and credit to the team for what we're doing.

"The goal and objective is to win the Champions League, to win the Premier League, to win everything. That's what the manager wants. That's what the fans want. That's what we as players want, too."

- Eberechi Eze on Arsenal competition: 'If you don't want to play you're not in the right place'

- Arsenal showed strength in depth in Lille win, but Gyökeres is a concern

And pressed as to whether he believes Arsenal are in a position to do that this season, the Spain international replied: "Absolutely. This is our mentality and the aim.

"We were so, so close last season. That proved to us that we are ready for it. Now it's about details. It's about being present and ready in the right moments, and of course we believe that."

Arsenal will bid to extend their winning run in the group phase to 15 when they travel to Germany to face Bayern Munich next week.

Before then, the Premier League champions will take on Nottingham Forest at the City Ground with midfielder Martín Zubimendi likely to be back in contention after he suffered an ankle injury in a training session following Arsenal's win against Leeds last weekend.

Piero Hincapié also suffered an ankle issue during the post-win training session at the Emirates Stadium.

"Zubi is much, much better," said Arteta. "Piero is improving, but it looks more significant. I think it will be a matter of weeks [before he is available], but we don't know exactly how many."

articles.headline: New era begins as Jayson Tatum and the Celtics embark on 1st season without Jaylen Brown
articles.description:
Boston Celtics 
              Last season: 58-26, lost to Philadelphia in first round of playoffs.
articles.body:
Boston Celtics 
              Last season: 58-26, lost to Philadelphia in first round of playoffs.


              COACH: Joe Mazzulla (5th season, 238-90).


              SEASON OPENER: Oct. 20 at Detroit.


              DEPARTURES: F Jaylen Brown, C Nikola Vucevic, F Anfernee Simons.


              ADDITIONS: F Paul George, C Mitchell Robinson, G Mike Conley Jr. 


              What to expect 
              It's a new era in Boston following the offseason trade of Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers. Only a few pieces remain from the core of the Celtics 2023-24 championship team. And there are lots of questions surrounding how this new version of the team will look without the homegrown tandem of Brown and Tatum that literally grew into the pillars of the franchise. Mazzulla has proven an ability to get the best out of what he has to work with, as evidenced in how the team played without Tatum last season as he recovered from rupturing his right Achilles tendon 17 months ago. But this may be the biggest test of Mazzulla's tenure as he looks to not only integrate new pieces, but make adjustments to an offense that has previously relied so heavily on 3-point shooting.


              Strengths and weaknesses


              The good: It starts with Tatum, who looks to be fully back to himself physically after rehabiliation from his surgery caused him to miss all but 16 regular season games and then Game 7 of their playoff loss to the 76ers because of a knee stiffness. George also enters the season healthy and at age 36 is poised to build off his strong playoff performance with the 76ers last season. Robinson’s presence brings an instant upgrade in rim protection, while also giving this group some great depth and options at center. Neemias Queta will likely remain the starter, but with plenty of support from both Robinson and Luka Garza. 


              The not-so-good: Brown’s departure breaks up the dynamic between he and Tatum that worked so well for nine seasons and eventually netted Boston its 18th NBA title. George says he’s more than willing to yield to Tatum, but that will put the weight on Tatum’s shoulders to carry the team, a burden he hasn’t had to bear alone yet during his career. 


              Players to watch
              Derrick White has tweaked the mechanics of his shot after a rough shooting year and will get more opportunities with Brown gone. Payton Pritchard started a career-high 50 games and average career bests in points (17.0), assists (5.2) and rebounds (3.9) last season coming off winning NBA Sixth Man of the Year honors in 2024-25. Last season also showed that he plays better coming off the bench, a role he’s expected to remain in barring injuries. Hugo Gonzalez also looks more skilled and comfortable at the NBA level as he prepares for Year 2. 


              ------

articles.headline: Lisandro Martínez slams Man United hierarchy: Squad not Champions League quality
articles.description: Lisandro Martínez launched a stinging verbal attack on Manchester United's hierarchy, after a 2-0 Champions League defeat against Atlético Madrid.
articles.body:
MADRID -- Lisandro Martínez launched a stinging verbal attack on Manchester United's hierarchy, singling out director of football Jason Wilcox, after a 2-0 Champions League defeat against Atlético Madrid by saying the club failed to strengthen the squad sufficiently during the summer transfer window.

United suffered a third defeat in five games against Diego Simeone's team and with manager Michael Carrick winning just one of his last seven games, the pressure is growing on the former midfielder to save his job.

But Argentina defender Martínez said that the scrutiny should fall on Carrick's bosses rather than the manager or players for failing to invest in the summer.

United spent just £150 million on new signings -- significantly less than their Big Six rivals.

"Really poor. Really poor," Martínez told Amazon Prime after the game in Madrid. "I have to control myself a lot, but sometimes it is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment.

"We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well.

"Atlético have an amazing team and they deserve to win today.

"But I expect more [investment]. 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more, but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."

When asked about the pressure on Carrick, Martínez directly pointed to those upstairs at Old Trafford in terms of who should be facing questions.

- Martínez exposes Man United's harsh reality: Blame lies with top brass, not Carrick

- Man United could never contend for the Premier League title -- but they aren't so bad either

"You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager," Martínez said. "What about other areas? [looks up] I can't say more.

"Tonight it is easy to say the coach, easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas [points up].

"He [Carrick] does his best. Every season is different. You can't stay with what you did last season.

"The teams knows how you play, they know every detail, if you don't change next season is a big problem.

"Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team.

"It is annoying, disappointing coming here and I am not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here."

Carrick was later asked about his defender's fiery comments but refused to give his opinion, saying he had not seen it.

"I haven't seen it. After a game like this you come here to try and get something from the game and you are disappointed and can be emotional," he said.

"I have not seen it so I don't think it is the right time.

"We all care and show that in different ways but now is the time to be together and work through.

"As a group, I don't doubt the togetherness or their wanting to win. Looking at the results, you could be saying its deeply wrong, but that's not been the case.

articles.headline: Wemby, Spurs have 'clarity' after Finals loss but know 'nothing is guaranteed'
articles.description: The Spurs enter the season with expectations to return to the Finals after loss to the Knicks.
articles.body:
IT'S A MUGGY Sunday in September at Frost Bank Center, and San Antonio Spurs media day is still a little more than two weeks away.

As the sun peeks through the arena's east entrance, condensation trickles down the floor-to-ceiling windows, a testament to the 86% humidity outside and similar to the pressure cooker inside the building for fans vying for a spot on Victor Wembanyama's official handpicked Spurs supporters group: the Jackals.

"This is something that hasn't been done to this level," said Aidan Sterling, president of the Jackals. "All the people who weren't Jackals last year, all the new guys, I know there's nerves amongst them."

Jitters would set in for some of the returning Jackals, too. Because unless they earned designation as "pack leader," membership isn't guaranteed this season, just like the Spurs aren't assured a spot in the 2026-27 NBA Finals after last season's shocking run that ended a six-year postseason drought and captivated fans.

"There's a lot of competition," said one of the Jackals' pack leaders. "Being a part of it last season doesn't guarantee you a spot this year."

It's a reality the Spurs understand all too well when measuring prospects for the upcoming season against the gauntlet that is the NBA's Western Conference, not to mention a vastly improved East or the fact that no team has advanced to the Finals in consecutive seasons since the 2018-19 Golden State Warriors. It's why Wembanyama and the rest of the squad tread carefully when discussing the sky-high expectations thrust upon the club in the wake of a 28-win improvement and Finals appearance. Wembanyama turned heads going into last season when revealing the team's goal of advancing to the postseason as a top-six seed.

Then, at September's media day, Wembanyama mentioned, "I couldn't imagine better motivation" coming off a 4-1 series loss to the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals. The 22-year-old was the only Spur that day to openly discuss specifics regarding expectations for the upcoming season.

"We have some goals between us that we're going to keep between us as teammates," Wembanyama said. "We won the West last year. We don't want to do anything less this year. We want to be the first seed, and then we want to keep fighting for this top spot."

To do that, San Antonio plans to lean on process to spin success the way it has done for decades. It's the approach the Spurs used last season, focusing on internal improvement and the day-to-day to help them manage an 82-game regular season and an extended postseason.

In their minds, that's the only way to return to the game's grandest stage.

It's a methodology dating to former coach Gregg Popovich's 29-season tenure in which San Antonio established a South Texas dynasty that churned out five titles and a record-tying run of 22 consecutive playoff appearances.

articles.headline: Fulham's Arbeloa fined for ref comments after Man United draw
articles.description: Fulham's Álvaro Arbeloa was fined $33,200 and given a warning for his comments after a match against Man United that questioned the integrity of the referee.
articles.body:
Fulham manager Álvaro Arbeloa was fined £25,000 ($33,200) and given a warning Wednesday for his comments after a Premier League match against Manchester United after he claimed officials would "not let Manchester United lose."

Arbeloa accepted a charge that he "acted in an improper manner" with his remarks made following the 1-1 draw between the teams at Fulham's Craven Cottage on Sept. 20.

"I think all fouls for them," the Spaniard said at the time in reference to United, which had lost to Manchester City the previous weekend because of a contentious goal.

"Every decision was for them," Arbeloa said. "And I knew, I knew after the game against Man City that they don't let Manchester United lose here."

According to its written reasons published Wednesday, the independent commission investigating the incident "felt that those words suggested, not only that there was bias on the part of the match officials throughout the game on repeated occasions, but also that there may even have been an element of pre-meditation by them and/or others to try to make up for an error in a different match."

Arbeloa is in his first season with Fulham after leaving Real Madrid.

articles.headline: Andy Burnham: Man City owners didn't mention Premier League charges in meeting
articles.description: Andy Burnham has said Manchester City's owners and directors did not raise the Premier League's charges against the club when he met with them.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham has said Manchester City's owners and directors did not raise the Premier League's charges against the club when he met with them.

The Prime Minister said he was "very happy" to set out details of the meetings, after they were published on Monday.

Manchester City have been found guilty on all counts of breaching the Premier League's financial rules and "the majority of charges" relating to failing to co-operate with the league's investigation.

On Monday it was revealed Burnham had a formal meeting with Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak at an investment summit, chatted to him in the stands at former City captain Vincent Kompany's testimonial and was accompanied by staff from the club on official overseas visits.

- Man City 'deserved' trophies - PSG boss Luis Enrique on charges

- Football Regulator chair will quit if politics interferes with any Man City investigation

Burnham was asked about the meetings during Prime Minister's Questions by Conservative MP Jerome Mayhew (Broadland and Fakenham).

Mayhew said: "The Prime Minister sees himself as a man of candour.

"So will he tell the House, did anyone associated with the running of Manchester City Football Club raise the charges they were facing, and have now been found guilty of, either with him or any member of his team?"

Burnham said: "They did not raise those issues with me.

"I'm very happy, Mr Speaker, for everything to be set out in full.

"It is why I asked the Greater Manchester Combined Authority [GMCA], in response to a call from the Leader of the Opposition and others, to set out a full statement of my key dealings with the owners of Manchester City Football Club.

"That statement was published on Monday, and it includes the issues in the news today.

"That is the position."

Details of the Prime Minister's contacts with the scandal-hit club and its Abu Dhabi owners during his time as Greater Manchester mayor were released by the combined authority earlier this week.

Burnham had told MPs that "all of my dealings" with Manchester City's owners would be published.

A GMCA spokesman said: "In October 2021 Andy Burnham, in his role as mayor of Greater Manchester, had a formal meeting with Khaldoon Al Mubarak at the UK Government's Global Investment Summit arranged by the Department for International Trade.

"In his capacity as mayor, he was a guest of Manchester City at home matches on a small number of occasions, including attending Vincent Kompany's testimonial match in September 2019, where he met the chairman informally in the stands.

"These have been declared in the usual way.

"Also during his time as mayor, representatives of Greater Manchester sporting clubs would routinely join business delegations as part of mayoral international visits.

"This included representatives from Manchester United travelling to Austin and Dublin, Lancashire Cricket Club joining a delegation to India, and Manchester City staff supporting visits to China and Japan."

articles.headline: Lamine Yamal: Assist for Anthony Gordon in Barcelona win 'almost-rabona'
articles.description: Lamine Yamal christened his dribble leading to Anthony Gordon's goal against Galatasaray an "almost-rabona" as Barcelona ran out 4-1 winners in the Champions League game.
articles.body:
Lamine Yamal christened his dribble leading to Anthony Gordon's goal against Galatasaray an "almost-rabona" as Barcelona ran out 4-1 winners in the Champions League game.

Yamal, 19, didn't score in the victory in Istanbul but produced a stunning second half display, setting up Fermín López with a pinpoint cross before creating for Gordon.

The teenager shaped to do a rabona, tricking the defender, only to knock the ball towards the byline instead. He benefitted from a small ricochet, but reacted quickly to drive inside before assisting the England international.

"I don't know what to call it, it was an almost-rabona dribble," Yamal told Movistar after the game as he watched a replay of the goal.

"It came off well to set up Gordon, that's the main thing, that it was effective at the end of the day."

In a separate interview with CBS, Yamal told former Barça forward Thierry Henry he is always looking for new ways to create space.

"Recently, I have noticed that a lot of opponents, whenever I reach the byline, go to ground, so I saw the opportunity, went for it and it came off," he added. 

"I always try to faint to create space. If you can create a bit of space that way, it gives us [attackers] life. It was nice, but also effective, so I am very happy."

- Flick urges caution as Barcelona extend perfect start with Champions League win

- Champions League recap: Atleti beat Man United, Viking snatch point vs. Bayern

- Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid, Barcelona chase Spurs defender Porro

In 10 appearances for Barça this season, Yamal has now scored eight goals and laid on nine assists.

Barça coach Hansi Flick credited him with "changing the game" against Galatasaray as the Spanish champions recovered from going behind to run out convincing winners.

"In the second half he was fantastic, how he dominated the game, the last pass ... It's unbelievable what he's doing," Flick said in the post game news conference.

The victory in Türkiye was Barça's 10th in a row at the start of the current campaign -- eight in LaLiga and two in the Champions League.

During that time, they have netted a remarkable 43 goals, with Yamal saying they are laying the foundations for potentially historic season.

"Always," he told CBS when asked if Barça believe a Treble -- winning LaLiga, the Champions League and the Copa del Rey -- is possible this season.

"We're Barcelona, we're the best team in the world."

That claim will be tested over the next week as Barça travel to third-placed Real Betis in LaLiga on Saturday, face Paris Saint-Germain in France in the Champions League next Tuesday and then host Real Madrid in the first Clásico of the season the following Sunday.

articles.headline: Why are Shakhtar playing Champions League games at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge?
articles.description: Explaining why Ukrainian side Shakhtar Donetsk will play home Champions League games at Chelsea's stadium.
articles.body:
Shakhtar Donetsk will host AEK Athens in the Champions League on Wednesday but the game will be played nearly 1,700 miles from their Ukraine home.

Stamford Bridge, Chelsea's home stadium, will act as Shakhtar's home ground for their European fixtures this season.

ESPN breaks down why that's happening...

Why are Shakhtar playing at Stamford Bridge?

Shakhtar are based in the Ukrainian city of Donetsk.

But they haven't played at their home ground, the Donbas Arena, since 2014. This year, amid security reasons due to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, they were seeking a stadium for their four home fixtures in the league phase of the Champions League.

Shakhtar have recently played 'home' European fixtures in Poland, Slovenia and Germany and were linked with using Brentford's stadium this season, but ended up agreeing to play at Stamford Bridge.

FC Shakhtar said: "Playing our Champions League home matches at Stamford Bridge is a special opportunity for Shakhtar. We are grateful to Chelsea Football Club for the opportunity to host our games at this special venue. Stamford Bridge is one of the most famous stadiums in world football, with an incredible history and atmosphere. We are convinced that Shakhtar's matches in London will provide unforgettable emotions for Ukrainian and English fans."

The 2021 UK census states that approximately 19,000 Ukraine-born people live in London.

How does it affect Chelsea?

Chelsea have no European fixtures this season after finishing 10th in the Premier League last season.

The Blues even cited their "disappointing 2025-26 season and failure to qualify for European football" as part of their reasoning to welcome Shakhtar.

A Chelsea statement said: "FC Shakhtar have played in countries across Europe and we look forward to welcoming them to London for their Champions League campaign this year.

"We will be working with the Shakhtar team closely over the coming weeks to ensure that matchdays run safely and smoothly for their team and supporters."

What matches will Stamford Bridge host?

Shakhtar vs. AEK Athens, Oct. 14

Shakhtar vs. Sporting CP, Nov. 3

articles.headline: Walker Kessler impresses in preseason debut for Lakers
articles.description: Lakers center Walker Kessler made a strong first impression in his preseason debut Tuesday, finishing with 11 points on 4-for-6 shooting, nine rebounds, one block and one steal while playing only in the first half.
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS -- Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler made a strong first impression in his preseason debut Tuesday.

The big man had 11 points on 4-for-6 shooting, nine rebounds, one block and one steal in L.A.'s 101-89 loss to the Golden State Warriors, playing only in the first half.

"I mean, it was a lot of fun being out there again," Kessler said. "It's been so long. Before the game I was actually pretty nervous, to be honest. But getting out there and just playing with the guys, it was a blast."

It had been 347 days since Kessler last appeared in an NBA game on Oct. 31 of last season for the Utah Jazz before undergoing season-ending surgery to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder in November.

After an offseason sign-and-trade to L.A., when the Lakers committed two future unprotected first-round picks and two pick swaps on top of a four-year, $130 million contract to the 25-year-old, he had to wait a little longer.

In one of the first couple of days of training camp, he jammed his left pinkie finger on the backboard while attempting to block a shot and was sidelined for the Lakers' first three preseason games.

Kessler said he was held out for "precautionary" reasons, but by playing Tuesday, he will still have the chance to play in two exhibition games (including Friday at home against the Denver Nuggets) before the regular season begins against the Warriors on Oct. 22.

His impact Tuesday was immediate. In the 16 minutes Kessler was on the court, the Lakers outscored the Warriors by 15. In the 32 minutes he wasn't, Golden State outscored L.A. by 27.

"I think I have a certain presence on the floor, but I think my teammates around me did a great job of playing defense on the perimeter," Kessler said. "I think we shared the ball really well tonight ... especially in the first half. It was a lot of fun."

Lakers coach JJ Redick praised the effort of the five-year veteran.

"I think he's a great fit for our team," Redick said. "Thought he did a nice job of running the floor, crashing, had some terrific rebounds in traffic, protected the rim. Just really, really good first half from him."

It's an effort Redick expects to see whenever Kessler is in the game.

"The word I've used with him, the challenge, is just being relentless," Redick said. "Just in terms of the motor on both ends. Running the floor, diving, screening, crashing the glass."

The message has resonated with the Lakers' new man in the middle.

"JJ and I talked, and that's kind of what we came up with this year: 'relentless,'" Kessler said. "And for me, that means just crashing every time, trying to be a presence in the paint, inside, outside, play hard, don't take plays off, on the offensive end and defensive end. So that's going to be my goal for this year."
